verdict.rationale: Gusto publishes a per-endpoint API reference (e.g. webhook subscription, health check and time-off decline reference pages). It also publishes Postman collections for each API version, and a sandbox environment (api.gusto-demo.com) with auto-generated demo companies lets developers actually run requests. However, nothing shows the reference itself is interactive, so runnability depends on Postman or the sandbox rather than on in-page examples. Missing for 10: evidence of in-page "try it" execution in the reference, runnable code samples embedded per endpoint, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the reference experience.
